title: From Red Hot band to High Society Six to Stu Bergen's New Orleans style
summary: He explains choosing the Red Hot name, dropping it after the Druids raid, then High Society Six and finally his own name for hotel work.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: What about you called yourself Red Hot at one time and then the Society Six came out. How did that happen?

When I was a little kid I always did like Devil Ham. You know anything? Trademark is the Devil. And I said what can I do for a name that will be before the public in other subjects, other phases? Like a Red Hot sale going on. So I must have seen that one day. So I said Berg if you go ahead and take the name of Red Hot, every time somebody uses a Red Hot sale going on they'll be thinking of you and they'll tie it in. So I got Harold Dutter, drove me the Devil blowing the trumpet, dancing on the coals and all.

In fact, Dick, one of the reasons why I dropped that name after about four years, there was some band playing at the Druids. Now I don't want to get in trouble here. But the Druids was raided on the counter that was Indecent Dance and the something. And after it was raided it was in the paper. And then later on, I still have it, I find a hand bill that they throw around in your yard, music by a red hot band, Druids. And I know my kids were getting kind of old then. I said, well boy, that's one reason why you ought to get out of it. But I must have been pretty good at trying to make the public think I'm playing that music. And the next thing was, I'd go to try to book a pretty good formal wedding, whether the husband or the daddy would spend a lot of money on a trousseau and a couple of thousand dollars for this and that.
And a week and a half of your band, Red Hot and his Red Hot trumpet, it just didn't fit in.

So I said, well I'll tell you what I'll do. We'll go from the beer drinking department to the champagne department. I'll call the band the High Society Six. High Society tied in with the old jazz tune and then to be facetious about it, trying to get in with the silk stocking gang. So I thought I was killing two birds and one stone. And then I started playing hotels where I got to use eight men. So I've ditched the High Society Six. It's Stu Bergen and his New Orleans style music. And that's all I can do.
